content.intro: Raw and Interpolated Strings is lesson 129 in Modern C# Language Features. Strings and arrays are indexed sequences, but text is encoded and may contain multiple code units per user-perceived character. Check boundaries and avoid unintended copies.
content.why_it_matters: Modern syntax is useful only when the compiler and target framework support it; version context belongs beside examples. This lesson focuses on raw and interpolated strings and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.
